text:
Kevin: Heads-up — just got a customer report that their Private (VPC) deployment fell back to the hosted model variant during a maintenance window. They have egress strictly disabled to certain regions.
Anna: ugh. do we have a reproducible trace? which policy blocked the egress?
Kevin: log snippet from their control plane shows: ```policy=egress_whitelist; target_region=eu-west-1; dest=control.redwood.internal:443; allow=false``` then our router tried fallback to hosted-1 and timed out.
Mike: if the control plane can't egress to our config service, the routing decision can't consult the allowed-region map. we should have a local cached policy per-customer in the private control plane.
Lucy: agree — customers explicitly asked for zero-egress. that means the private runtime must make routing choices without calling back. we already have a compact policy blob in the agent, but it's missing model-variant fallbacks.
Kevin: proposal: extend the agent policy blob to include an ordered list of allowed model variants + region constraints and fallback prefs. runtime checks blob first; only if blob absent it calls control plane.
Anna: +1, but needs UX in Console to surface the active blob and a rollout preview. operations want a dry-run so they can see where requests would route if we change the fallback order.
console-bot: note: rollout preview feature request created: https://dash.redwood/rollouts/REQ-4321
Mike: edge case: what if the agent has stale blob and thinks eu-west is allowed but network rule changed? we need TTL + heartbeat.
Lucy: TTL is fine. also add a hard fail mode: if blob missing or expired, runtime returns 429 with special code (PRIV_EGRESS_BLOCK) instead of automatically egressing. safer for compliance.
Kevin: I like explicit failure over blind egress. customers asked for auditable events. include an audit event: ```{event: "fallback_attempt", reason: "egress_blocked", chosen: null}```
Anna: Console UI needs to show these audit events with quick filters: customer, timeframe, event_type. Also we should expose a per-customer toggle: allow_control_plane_query (true/false) so support can temporarily enable egress for debugging.
Mike: that toggle must be impossible to set via API unless signed by an admin role — we can't let devs flip it. add an approval workflow.
Lucy: telemetry note: for private installs with no egress, we still need aggregated metrics (latency/cost). we'll send anonymized usage pings via an opt-in channel or write collectors to customers' on-prem metrics if they agree.
sre-bot: incident digest: customer "AcmeHealth" reported 3 fallback attempts between 12:03-12:07 UTC; root cause: agent lacked fallback list. ticket #IN-1147 created.
Kevin: next steps I propose: 1) schema for local policy blob (YAML) 2) agent validation + TTL semantics 3) runtime behavior: consult blob -> apply fallback list -> if no allowed fallback return PRIV_EGRESS_BLOCK 4) Console UX: rollout preview + audit viewer + admin toggle workflow.
Anna: can someone draft the blob schema? I'll put a Console mock in Figma.
Mike: quick sketch of the blob (WIP): ```
version: 1
customer_id: acme-123
allowed_regions: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]
model_fallbacks:
  - name: redwood-mini-quant
    regions: [eu-west-1]
    priority: 10
  - name: redwood-small-fp16
    regions: [eu-central-1, eu-west-1]
    priority: 20
ttl_seconds: 3600
last_issued: 2026-01-10T11:22:33Z
allow_control_plane_query: false
```
Lucy: nice. also include a field `audit_level` (off/minimal/verbose) so private installs can opt-in to detailed audit events.
Kevin: Implementation owners? Mike + Lucy for agent/runtime, Anna for Console UX, I'll coordinate API and release notes.
Anna: timeline?
Kevin: aim for alpha in 3 sprints. we push a patch to runtime (PR link coming) that returns explicit error instead of egressing, then follow with Console rollout preview.
Lucy: I'll add unit tests for blob TTL and for the fallback decision tree.
Mike: I'll prototype the on-agent validation and a CLI tool to generate a blob for customers that run air-gapped installs.
